name: gupnp-tools
desc: Free replacements of Intel's UPnP tools
why: A door into UPnP discovery and device control, a protocol running on most home routers that few people ever inspect.

brief.what_it_is: GUPnP Tools is a set of free command-line replacements for Intel's UPnP tools, built on the GUPnP library. According to its GitLab page, it provides client and server side tools for testing and debugging UPnP devices and control points. The package ships six executables: gssdp-discover, gupnp-av-cp, gupnp-event-dumper, gupnp-network-light, gupnp-universal-cp, and gupnp-upload. The fetched text does not describe what each one takes in or emits, so the writer should not infer those details from the names.
brief.why_it_exists: The project positions itself as a free alternative to Intel's proprietary UPnP tools. Its stated purpose is to let people easily test and debug their UPnP devices and control points.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond brew install was seen in the fetched pages. No runtime, account, hardware, or first-run steps were mentioned. The brew caveats field is empty.
brief.standout: It is a GNOME-hosted, GPL-licensed open replacement for a vendor's UPnP debugging tools, which makes UPnP discovery and device control inspectable without Intel's software. The scout's note that UPnP runs on most home routers is the scout's framing and does not appear in the pages I fetched.
brief.status: unknown. The GitLab page shows a creation date of May 25, 2018, but no release or last-commit date was visible in the fetched text. The GNOME wiki homepage says that site has been retired and points to gitlab.gnome.org for current information, so the GitLab repository is the live home.
brief.caveats: The homepage at wiki.gnome.org/GUPnP/ is a retired wiki archive stub with no project content; I relied on the GitLab page for the description. The fetched GitLab text was short and contained no command examples, usage instructions, or README body, so the executables' behavior is unverified. The license is GNU GPL v2.0 or later. The router claim in the scout notes was not confirmed by any page I read.
